chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Sukuni narrated from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, who said: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated from his father, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

As for sheep, if you face them, they face you, and if you turn away, they turn away; and as for cows, if you face them, they face you, and if you turn away, they turn away; and camels are the bridles of the devils, if you face them, they turn away, and if you turn away, they turn away, and their goodness does not come except from their most ill-omened side. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, then who will take them after this? He said: Then where are the wretched and dissolute? Salih said: And Isma'il ibn Mihran recited: It is wealth; were it not for the littleness of its decrease that surrounds it, whoever wishes will circle with it, and whoever wishes will sell it.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of camels being described as the 'bridles of the devils' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the camel's stubborn nature as a metaphor for the 'bridles of devils,' illustrating how wealth can become a spiritual obstacle if not managed with wisdom. The accompanying verse by Isma'il ibn Mihran underscores the transient nature of material possessions, urging believers to view wealth as a test rather than an end. This narration aligns with Shia ethical teachings on detachment from worldly goods and the practical management of assets.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Ali bin Ahmad bin Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Abi Abdillah al-Sukuni, from Saleh bin Abi Hammad, that he said: We were told by Isma’eel bin Mahran, from his father, from Amru bin Abi’l-Miqdam, from Abu Abdillah, Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, from his fathers, from Ali, peace be upon them, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said:

With regards to sheep, if you come forward, they come forward, and if you return, they return, and with regards to cows, if you come forward, they come forward, and if you return, they return. Camels, however, are the interpositions of devils; if you come forward, they return, and if you return, they return, and their goodness does not come except from their most ill-omened side. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, then who will take them after this? He said: Then where are the wretched and dissolute? Saleh said: Isma’eel bin Mahran recited: It is property; were it not for the littleness of its decrease that surrounds it. Hence, the one who wishes, will circle with it, and the one who wishes, will sell it.
